subject.title: Bug: isRecurringTopOfHourCronExpr fails to match cron expressions with step values

question: Should OpenClaw stagger every schedule that includes minute zero, or only schedules that are primarily top-of-hour-like and not every-minute/non-dividing step expressions?
rationale: Current source clearly misses the reported step/list/range forms, but the issue discussion shows unresolved semantics for wildcard, every-minute, and non-dividing step expressions that affect user-visible scheduling behavior.

options.title: Adopt minute-zero semantics
options.body: Treat any valid minute field that includes minute zero as eligible for the default top-of-hour stagger and cover step, list, range, wildcard, and 6-field forms in tests.

options.title: Exclude high-frequency schedules
options.body: Fix `*/15`, `0,30`, and ranges starting at zero while explicitly excluding `*`, `*/1`, and other high-frequency expressions from top-of-hour staggering.

options.title: Close the linked PR and defer
options.body: Keep the issue open as a product decision until maintainers choose the exact cron semantics and implementation boundary.

recommendation.title: Adopt minute-zero semantics
recommendation.body: Treat any valid minute field that includes minute zero as eligible for the default top-of-hour stagger and cover step, list, range, wildcard, and 6-field forms in tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current cron stagger helper and tests, so they are the clearest history-based owner for deciding the intended scheduling semantics.
